summary: # Marvelous Designer 2024 Tutorial: Making a Ruffled Skirt ## Introduction Hello everyone! Today, we are going to make a Heyebian half-body skirt. This skirt consists of three pieces, and we will learn how to fold the skirt version and create the Heyebian version. Additionally, we will learn how to improve the quality of clothing and how to use the right fabric for it. ## Downloading the Ruffle Skirt Base File First of all, please download the Ruffle Skirt Base file provided by the Marvelous Designer team in the Connect store. You can find the link in the top comment to download the file. This file includes a top, pants, and belt version. ## Creating the Half-Body Skirt As the basis of the skirt, we want to create a half-body skirt and then add multi-layered Heyebian details to it. ### Step 1: Using the Circle Tool In the 2D window, select the circle tool. At the same time, press the Shift and Ctrl keys, then click and drag the mouse to create the center with the initial click position. By using the center of the belt as the initial point and dragging the mouse, we can estimate the length of the skirt that is created at the end. ### Step 2: Modifying the Skirt Shape Delete the left side to make the skirt a half-circle. In the front position, we will create the waistline of the skirt version. Use the plus point division tool to refer to the pink smart guide line to create the endpoint on the middle line. Select the inner circle tool, click the endpoint, then drag the mouse to create the waistline. ### Step 3: Merging the Skirt and Belt Versions Press Shift and Ctrl keys again to click the center position to create the inner circle. Use the free-form tool to merge the skirt version and the belt version together. ## Positioning the Skirt in 3D In the 3D window, place the skirt version in a position that does not interlace with the virtual model and then start modeling. Since the inner skirt is frozen, even if the skirt interlaces with it, the effect is relatively small. Later, we will remove the excess part of the skirt version. ## Adjusting the Waistline After selecting the middle skirt, drag the selection box to search for the skirt version until the length is suitable. To create the waistline skirt version, select the half-circle skirt version and choose the 3D arrangement position for selection. This makes it more convenient to sew and model the waistline directly on the flat skirt. ### Step 4: Creating Internal Lines Select the waistline and skirt line. Using the curve generation function, create two internal lines for the lining, as this will be more convenient. ### Step 5: Creating Cross-Sectional Strips Next, let's create a cross-sectional strip. Use the internal line diameter table. Based on the internal lines created, add additional internal lines. These internal lines will form a cross-sectional strip, and I will set the diameter value to 20mm. ### Step 6: Adjusting Cross-Sectional Strips Now we are going to create another internal line on the opposite side. Maintain the same diameter value and select the reverse option. Use the outer cross-sectional strip to create a new strip. The strip created will automatically arrange above the original strip in the 3D window, and a line will automatically be created between the two strips. ### Step 7: Disconnecting and Trimming Use the disconnect function to remove the link between the two strips. Select the internal line to form the cross-sectional strip and select cut-off. Delete the excess strips, keeping only the cross-sectional strip. Freeze the cross-sectional strip and adjust its size as needed. ## Simulation and Final Adjustments Open the simulation. If you think the cross-sectional fold is too much or too little, you can press Ctrl-Z to return to the pre-monitoring state and re-adjust the size of the cross-sectional strip. If you want to adjust the width of the cross-sectional strip, you can select the outer strip and adjust it according to your needs. ### Step 8: Shrinking the Cross-Sectional Strip To shrink the cross-sectional strip, change the direction option from extension to shrink and set the width value accordingly. After confirming, you will see that the cross-sectional strip becomes narrower. When the particle diameter is smaller, the cross-sectional strip will appear more natural and detailed. ## Finalizing the Skirt Design Remove any excess sewing lines. Create a line to sew on the waist, ensuring the thickness is set to 1. Select the half-group panels and create a symmetrical panel, placing it in the upper-right window. Then, create the line between the symmetrical panels and merge the left and right groups together. Delete any excess points if necessary and merge the horizontal panel panels together. ### Step 9: Simulation of the Seam Line Open the simulation and wait for the half-group panels to simulate. After the simulation is completed, copy and paste all the half-group panels and arrange them in the 2D and 3D windows. In the 3D window, rotate the panels appropriately to align the side lines. ### Step 10: Applying Elasticity Now, we will apply elasticity to the fold position by applying it to the nuclear edge seam line for a more realistic shrink effect. After opening the simulation, if you want to modify the elasticity ratio, you can press Ctrl-Z to go back to the selection of these lines and enter a new value. ### Final Touches We will apply a new fabric to the half-group plate and modify its physical properties to achieve the desired look. ## Conclusion This is the final semi-permanent effect, and this concludes our tutorial. Thank you for watching! See you in the next video.
